name: loglook
description: Small read-only viewer and API for the syslog files Unraid's built-in syslog server collects (syslog-IP.log and its rotated copies). Pick a device and a time window and loglook finds the lines by their own timestamps across the live and rotated files, so you never open a multi-gigabyte file by hand. Three views of any window: the lines, top patterns (MACs, IPs and numbers collapsed so repeats become one row with a count) and counts per captured value. Filters take plain text or a regex, and a window can end earlier to compare today with previous days. A read-only JSON API behind bearer tokens serves the same queries to scripts and automations such as n8n. Tokens are created in the web UI, shown once, and stored hashed. Setup: set Syslog Folder to your Unraid syslog share (Settings, Syslog Server, Local syslog folder). Open the web UI, create the admin user, then open Sources: every device that has written a log appears with a Name it box, and the timezone is set on the same page. Nothing to write by hand. The log folder is mounted read-only and nothing in it is ever changed. Web interface: http://Unraid_IP:8000

paths.name: Syslog Folder
paths.description: The folder your syslog server writes to (files named syslog-IP.log). Mounted read-only.

paths.name: Config
paths.description: Where the Sources page keeps device names and the timezone (sources.yml). Must be writable; created on first save.

paths.name: Data
paths.description: The admin login, API tokens and the generated session key. Keep on persistent storage.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: Port for the web interface and the API.

variables.name: Secret Key
variables.description: Optional. Signs the login cookie. Leave empty and a random key is generated on first start and kept in the Data folder.

variables.name: Secure Cookies
variables.description: Set to true only when you reach loglook over HTTPS (a reverse proxy such as Traefik terminates TLS). The login does not work over plain HTTP while this is on.
